response.sql: WITH rating_stats AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS per_day_price FROM film GROUP BY rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(per_day_price) AS mean_per_day FROM rating_stats), above AS (SELECT rs.avg_length, rs.per_day_price, rs.per_day_price - o.mean_per_day AS excess FROM rating_stats rs CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE rs.per_day_price > o.mean_per_day) SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS avg_length, AVG(per_day_price) AS avg_per_day_price, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: The database is MySQL (the schema uses MySQL types such as UNSIGNED and TINYINT), so the WITH clauses need MySQL 8.0 or later.

AVG(length) skips NULL lengths, which satisfies 'ignoring films with no length'. Films with NULL length still count toward the rating's rental_rate and rental_duration averages, because the per-day price uses all films in each rating.
'Average of their average lengths' and 'average of their per-day prices' are unweighted means over the qualifying ratings, each rating counting once, as the request states.

The 'average amount by which their per-day price exceeds the cross-rating mean' is the mean of (per_day_price - mean_per_day) over the qualifying ratings. This equals the average per-day price minus the mean, so it has the same meaning under either reading.
No rounding is applied, as requested. The divisions use MySQL's exact decimal arithmetic.
